labels.label: infra:developing-theorem-344 (no ledger label; RamcovGX.tex:344, commented out)

hypotheses.note: D is required to be a (G,X)-morphism (developing map); for bare equivariant maps uniqueness is false (counterexample formalized)

findings: RamcovGX.tex:344 (commented out) asks only for 'a map D : M~ -> X which is rho-equivariant'. Read literally, existence is trivial (a constant map with rho = 1) and the uniqueness 'such couples only differ by conjugation' is false: on the simply connected line with its translation structure, (id, 1) and (const 0, 1) are both equivariant couples and no translation relates them (GX.developing_unique_fails_for_bare_maps). The true statement needs D to be a local (G,X)-isomorphism / (G,X)-morphism; with that, uniqueness holds with a UNIQUE g, dev' = g.dev and hol' = g hol g^-1 (GX.developing_unique). Should the line be restored, it wants 'a (G,X)-morphism (developing map) D'.

kb_proposals: The developing map is a SECTION of the etale space of germs GX.DevSpace G X N (points <x,g> = germ of g . chartAt X x, basic sets B(c,U)); it is a covering trivial over each chart domain (GX.DevSpace.isCoveringMap_pt), so Mathlib's IsCoveringMap.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts gives existence on a simply connected base and IsCoveringMap.eq_of_comp_eq gives uniqueness with NO Hausdorff hypothesis on X.
letI in a theorem STATEMENT is inlined at elaboration (no let survives in the goal): prove such a statement with letI := <same instance> in the proof, never intro.
Inside namespace GX, while declaring IsGXMorphism.foo, a bare eq_of_eqOn resolves to IsGXMorphism.eq_of_eqOn: write GX.eq_of_eqOn.
